newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia first half deficit C$600 million.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia first half deficit C$600 million.

text.p: British Columbia said Friday that its budget deficit in the first half of the 1996/97 fiscal year was about C$600 million, C$330 million higher than forecast.

The government said revenue for the six months to September 30 was C$9.6 million, while spending was C$10.2 billion. It blamed the bigger than expected deficit on a revenue shortfall due to lower commodity prices and a softening in the economy. The deficit compared with a deficit of C$60 million in the first half of last year.
The province said total net debt for the government, Crown corporations and agencies fell C$866 million to C$27.8 billion during the period.
At September 30, direct provincial government debt totalled C$10.8 billion, up C$534 million from the end of March.

The government also gave final figures for the 1995/96 year, showing a deficit of C$369 million. This was in line with figures provided by the provincial finance minster earlier this month, but up from the government's preliminary figure of C$235 million.
